messages.subject: Re: Cooler and moister mesoclimatic conditions, but warmer and drier microclimatic conditions at the same time?
messages.subject_clean: Cooler and moister mesoclimatic conditions, but warmer and drier microclimatic conditions at the same time?
messages.body_plain:
So, if I understand, micro_ncep does adjust the effect of different rainfall or cloud cover values between NCEP pixels on mesoclimatic conditions (eg., TAREF) but not for microclimatic conditions (eg., TALOC)? I mean mesoclimatic conditions as the downscaled climate data of NCEP to 30m pixels (setted scale of digital elevation data) and microclimatic conditions as a point.
Thanks a lot.

El lunes, 30 de noviembre de 2020 a las 15:06:22 UTC-6, Michael Kearney escribió:
> Hi Israel,
>
> To really work out what's going on, you'd have to compare the inputs and outputs at particular sites, e.g. two contrasting sites from your two zones. More generally, the NCEP data is at ~2 degrees resolution and you're looking at points within about 0.5 degrees so you may have one or two pixels of NCEP depending on where the points lie on the grid. That means that you may have a sudden jump in the variables that aren't being adjusted by the micro_ncep function, e.g. rainfall, cloud cover. Differences in cloud cover are the most likely reason you'd see a higher microclimatic temperature at a site with a lower 2m air temp. I see you're using NDVI as maximum shade - it isn't really a measure of shade but would be proportional to shade. Be careful comparing relative humidity - it's a function of temperature. Better to compute vapour pressure (use the WETAIR function) to see if the air is truly moister.
>
> Re the ectotherm model - try turning all behaviour off and see what you get. Also, some notes on the parameters you've used:
>
> fossorial = 0 # this isn't properly implemented yet so don't turn it on
>
> rainact = 1 # you have set activity to be limited by rainfall which could also be affecting your Tb estimates, depending on whether you have more than one pixel of NCEP data overlapping
>
>
> All the parameters below are relevant only if the DEB model is running
>
> T_REF= 34.2+273.15, # soilnode = 1, eggshade = 1, T_L = 30.6+273.15, T_H = 36.4+273.15, stage = 2, viviparous = 0, photostart = 4, photofinish = 1, photodirs = 0
> Hope that helps,
> Mike
> On Monday, November 30, 2020 at 10:35:52 PM UTC+11 biolog...@gmail.com wrote:
> >
> > Hello everyone, I would like to ask for an apparent contradiction between mesoclimate and microclimatic variables calculated with micro_ncep and ectotherm variables calculated with ectotherm.
> >
> > I calculated data for 105 points between two adjacent zones (A and B). Zone A had a higher altitude, vegetation cover (estimated as NDVI), as well as lower temperature and relative humidity in mesoclimatic conditions (TAREF and RH [2m]). However, the same zone A resulted in higher microclimatic temperature and relative humidity (TALOC and RHLOC [0.03cm]), as well as higher body temperature (TC) and substrate (TSUB), greater use of shade (SHADE), and higher metabolism (O2_ml).
> >
> >  I analyzed the substrate temperature at a 30m scale with a substrate temperature raster obtained via MODIS. We found that for the same study points, the substrate temperature was higher in zone B than in A, contrary to the microclimatic—but consistent with the mesoclimatic—results obtained with NicheMapR.
> >
> > So my question is how can mesoclimatic conditions be cooler and moister in zone A, but at the same time, microclimatic conditions be hotter and drier in the same zone?
> >
> > I attach an example to obtain data for 10 geographic points by each zone (IVE_Template_301120). In the database, zone A refers to DENTRO and B to NORTE. Since I am controlling for the effect of climate differences, I compare two years with different vegetation cover but experiencing the climate conditions of the hottest year in Mexico (2017).
> >
> > Thank you very much for your time.

messages.subject: Re: Cooler and moister mesoclimatic conditions, but warmer and drier microclimatic conditions at the same time?
messages.subject_clean: Cooler and moister mesoclimatic conditions, but warmer and drier microclimatic conditions at the same time?
messages.body_plain:
Hi Israel,

micro_ncep uses microclima to adjust the NCEP air temperature (and relative humidity) for terrain effects, thereby disaggregating it to a degree (e.g. lapse-rate correction as well as cold air drainage and coastal effects if you turn those on). Then the microclimate (TALOC, soil temps, etc.) are computed based on the adjusted NCEP inputs as well as the terrain and habitat effects (e.g. slope, shade). But the incoming rainfall, cloud cover, downwelling longwave radiation (= sky temperature) and wind speed are all remaining at the NCEP resolution. Hope that makes sense. You can read more about it in

Kearney, M.R., Gillingham, P.K., Bramer, I., Duffy, J.P. & Maclean, I.M.D. (2020). A method for computing hourly, historical, terrain-corrected microclimate anywhere on earth. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 11, 38–43.

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Dynamic Energy Budget theory introduction
messages.body_plain:
Dear NicheMapR users,

As you probably know, the NicheMapR package uses models derived from the Dynamic Energy Budget (DEB) theory for computing growth, development and reproduction.

DEB is a powerful but conceptually challenging theory and it took me a long time to digest it and then apply it. I recently wrote an overview of metabolic theory <https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/brv.12668> which puts the DEB theory into context with the 'von Bertalanffy' growth model and the 'metabolic theory of ecology', which may help you digest DEB further. Writing it certainly helped me!

DM me if you'd like a copy.

All the best,
Mike

messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,

Yes it's the area receiving direct solar radiation when the animal has oriented itself perpendicular to the sun. The relevant code in the model is:

QSDIR=ABSAN*ASIL*(1.00-PDIF)*QNORM*(1.0-(SHADE/100.))

and ASIL will vary as a thermoregulatory strategy during basking in the model.

Or, if you are running it with live = 0, you can vary the input 'postur':

postur = 1, postural orientation to sun, 1 = perpendicular, 2 = parallel, 0 = half way between

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Cooler and moister mesoclimatic conditions, but warmer and drier microclimatic conditions at the same time?
messages.subject_clean: Cooler and moister mesoclimatic conditions, but warmer and drier microclimatic conditions at the same time?
messages.body_plain:
Hi, the reason for this answer is to find out about an idea that may you have given the resolutions of your two observations.
1.-All points rely on one pixel of cloud cover and air temperature of NCEP-R2 (pictures).
2.-Turning off behavioral adjustments (burrow, climb, shade_seek=0), set the ectotherm as inanimated (live=0) and match cases relative to its year (1999), season (dry season) and vegetation cover (NDVI%) do not change the pattern: cooler mesoclimate but hotter microclimate in zone A, and viceverza in zone B.
Study site its in a seasonal tropical dry forest in dry season, so it does not rain.
If I do not find out what's going on, I thinl I should use mesoclimatic data (TAREF) because it matches patterns of mesoclimatic data of other sources (MODIS: TSUB at 30m scale).
Me and my team are confussed because NicheMapR data does match observed temporal phenomena (ie., yearly and seasonal mesoclimatic and microclimatic conditions), but give us apparently contradicted spatial phenomena (ie., mesoclimatic and microclimatic data between study sites).

Thank you very much for your time.

 Total cloud cover. From NCEP-R2 (tcdc.eatm.gauss.1999)
 Maximum air temperature at 2m. From NCEP-R2 (tmax.2m.gauss.1999)

messages.subject: Re: custom shape coefficients
messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,

You can certainly get the rough dimensions from photos if you're using a generic shape, but note that 'shape_a' etc. parameters are not used if shape > 3 (lizard, frog or custom) and instead parameters from regressions of measured surface area with size are used, e.g. the relevant Fortran code is pasted below from within the 'GEOM.f' subroutine for the frog and the custom shape. The measurements for the frog are described in Tracy's 1976 paper in Ecological Monographs.

All the best,
Mike

      IF(GEOMETRY.EQ.4)THEN
C      AREA OF LEOPARD FROG (C.R. TRACY 1976 ECOL. MONOG.)
       ATOTAL=(12.79*GMASS**.606)/10000.
       AV=(0.425*GMASS**.85)/10000.
       ATOT=ATOTAL
C      NORMAL AND POINTING @ SUN SILHOUETTE AREA: EQ'N 11 TRACY 1976
       ZEN=0.
       PCTN=1.38171E-06*ZEN**4-1.93335E-04*ZEN**3.+
     & 4.75761E-03*ZEN**2.-0.167912*ZEN+45.8228
       ASILN=PCTN*ATOT/100.
       ZEN=90.
       PCTP=1.38171E-06*ZEN**4-1.93335E-04*ZEN**3.+
     & 4.75761E-03*ZEN**2.-0.167912*ZEN+45.8228
       ASILP=PCTP*ATOT/100.
       AREA=ATOT
       AV=AREA*PTCOND
       AT=AREA*SKINT
       IF(PANT.GT.1)THEN
        AEFF=(SKINW+PMOUTH)*AREA-SKINW*AREA*PTCOND-SKINW*AREA*SKINT
       ELSE
        AEFF=SKINW*AREA-SKINW*AREA*PTCOND-SKINW*AREA*SKINT
       ENDIF
      ENDIF

C     USER-DEFINED GEOMETRY
      IF(GEOMETRY.EQ.5) THEN
       ATOTAL=(CUSTOMGEOM(1)*GMASS**CUSTOMGEOM(2))/10000.
       AV=(CUSTOMGEOM(3)*GMASS**CUSTOMGEOM(4))/10000.
       ATOT=ATOTAL
       VOL=AMASS/ANDENS
C      CONDUCTION - RADIATION, ETC DIMENSION. ASSUME L=2D=4R1;
C      THEN VOL=PI*R1**2*L = 4*PI*R1**3
       R1=(VOL/(4.*PI))**(1./3.)
C      NORMAL AND POINTING @ SUN SILHOUETTE AREA: PORTER & TRACY 1984
C      USER MUST DEFINE MAX. SILHOUETTE AREA (NORMAL TO THE SUN)
       ASILN=(CUSTOMGEOM(5)*GMASS**CUSTOMGEOM(6))/10000.
C      USER MUST DEFINE MIN. SILHOUETTE AREA (POINTING TOWARD THE SUN)
       ASILP=(CUSTOMGEOM(7)*GMASS**CUSTOMGEOM(8))/10000.
       AREA=ATOT
       AV=AREA*PTCOND
       AT=AREA*SKINT
       IF(PANT.GT.1)THEN
        AEFF=(SKINW+PMOUTH)*AREA-SKINW*AREA*PTCOND-SKINW*AREA*SKINT
       ELSE
        AEFF=SKINW*AREA-SKINW*AREA*PTCOND-SKINW*AREA*SKINT
       ENDIF
      ENDIF

messages.subject: changing burrowing behavior in Fortran
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

In part inspired by the new paper of Huey et al in Ecology Letters, and in part because I am working in a ridiculously cold place right now (Czechia), I am trying to change behavioral strategies for animals sheltered in burrows. The idea is that an animal would select different depths if trying to maximize physiological performance (higher temperatures), saving energy (lower temperatures), or any other strategy you might think of.

To achieve that I have added a new argument (burrowbhv) and modified the SELDEP.f subroutine like this:

       DO 13 IDEP=MINNODE,NON
C     normal behavior in NicheMapR
         IF(BURROWBHV.EQ.0)THEN
            MAXTEMP=(CTMAX-(CTMAX-TMAXPR)/2.)
            IF((TSOIL(IDEP).GT.CTMIN).AND.(TSOIL(IDEP).LT.MAXTEMP))THEN
                TA = TSOIL(IDEP)
                RELHUM = HSOIL(IDEP)*100.
                NEWDEP = ZSOIL(IDEP)
             ENDIF
C      energy conservation: selecting low temperatures (between CTmin and Temerge)
          ELSE IF(BURROWBHV.EQ.1)THEN
             IF((TSOIL(IDEP).GT.CTMIN).AND.(TSOIL(IDEP).LE.TEMERGE))THEN
                TA = TSOIL(IDEP)
                RELHUM = HSOIL(IDEP)*100.
                NEWDEP = ZSOIL(IDEP)
             ENDIF
C      optimum performance strategy (between Temerge and Tpref)
          ELSE IF(BURROWBHV.EQ.2)THEN
             IF((TSOIL(IDEP).GT.TEMERGE).AND.(TSOIL(IDEP).LE.TPREF))THEN
                TA = TSOIL(IDEP)
                RELHUM = HSOIL(IDEP)*100.
                NEWDEP = ZSOIL(IDEP)
             ENDIF
           ENDIF
           GO TO 999
13     CONTINUE

However, even if I run the ectotherm model with burrowbhv=0, which should be equal to running the ectotherm model with the official NicheMapR package, I am getting different results. Basically, animals retreat to a depth of 2.5 cm, and stay there all the time they are burrowed. This results in ery low and very high TCs, way out of their tolerance range. In contrast, with the official NicheMapR they retreat to deeper nodes to avoid surpassing CTmin and CTmax.

I am not seeing any evident problem in my code but, again, I am not a Fortran expert and I might be making some stupid mistake...

Thanks a lot in advance! All the best,
Urtzi

messages.body_plain:
Hi Urtzi,

I dug deeper into your code :) and spotted that you put 'goto 999' at the end of the code within the loop through the depths, so it's just exiting after the first depth. You need to put the goto statement after each ' NEWDEP = ZSOIL(IDEP)'. Then it won't exit the loop until the criterion is met (but note that this approach takes the shallowest depth matching the criteria, even if there might be suitable conditions deeper down).

All the best,
Mike

messages.subject: Re: Burrow clarification
messages.body_plain:
Hi Adam,

Yes 'burrowing' means moving below the surface (could be into a crevice too, not necessarily actively burrowing) and the model will try this as a thermoregulatory strategy if you have allowed it, if it has exhausted all other options for being surface-active. What I just said doesn't apply for when the Dynamic Energy Budget model has been turned on, however. In that case, the animal will retreat to its burrow if it has a sufficiently full stomach, unless it would be able to be closer to its preferred temperature out of its burrow.

All the best,
Mike
